answer: A delayed-activation lock resists cheap Sybil floods. A new key must sit on a public trellis of pending identities for many epochs, with a bond frozen the whole time, before it can vote or earn. Neighbors may flag clones during that wait, and any proven duplicate loses the bond. An attacker who wants a grove of a thousand voters must pre-fund a thousand separate bonds and idle through the queue, tying up capital that could have been used elsewhere. Each activation is a signed, time-stamped quill mark that cannot be backdated, so minting fresh wallets overnight grants no immediate influence.
